BaseRecord.description: The fields every record has, and the evidence any record may cite.

evidence.description: Links to sources outside this site that back up what the record says, such as the pull requests behind a contribution or a page its description mentions, e.g. "https://github.com/hdmf-dev/hdmf/pull/672". What a GitHub pull request or issue is (its title and state) is fetched from GitHub rather than written here.

record_version.description: Version of the record's own content, bumped whenever the record changes.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written against. The record may still be valid under other schema versions; this names the version at the time it was written.

tags.description: Keywords for the topics, methods and technologies of the work, each a theme:tag pair from the vocabulary in schemas/tags.yaml, e.g. "standards:NWB".

BaseRecord.title: BaseRecord

Dataset.description: A dataset, or collection of datasets, curated for publication and the role held in curating it. Each record is one JSON file under datasets/.

built_with.description: Other records of the software this work was built with, such as a project it depends on directly or the one that converted a dataset, e.g. "projects/neuroconv".

description.description: Paragraphs of plain text describing the curation work, in which **double asterisks** mark emphasis.

evidence.description: Links to sources outside this site that back up what the record says, such as the pull requests behind a contribution or a page its description mentions, e.g. "https://github.com/hdmf-dev/hdmf/pull/672". What a GitHub pull request or issue is (its title and state) is fetched from GitHub rather than written here.

group.description: Research group that produced the data, e.g. "Leifer Lab".

institution.description: Institution the group belongs to, e.g. "Princeton University". Omitted for groups that span several institutions.

name.description: Title of the dataset or collection.

record_version.description: Version of the record's own content, bumped whenever the record changes.

role.description: Role held in curating the data, e.g. "Primary Engineer" or "Supervisor".

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written against. The record may still be valid under other schema versions; this names the version at the time it was written.

tags.description: Keywords for the topics, methods and technologies of the work, each a theme:tag pair from the vocabulary in schemas/tags.yaml, e.g. "standards:NWB".

Dataset.title: Dataset

DatasetLinks.description: Resources related to a dataset, keyed by type.

code.description: Source code that converted the data to a standard format.

dataset.description: The published data, e.g. a Dandiset on the DANDI Archive.

manuscript.description: The associated publication, ideally as a DOI link.

notebook.description: Jupyter Notebook(s) demonstrating how to access and analyze the data.

DatasetLinks.title: DatasetLinks

Project.description: A software project and the role held on it. Each record is one JSON file under projects/.

built_with.description: Other records of the software this work was built with, such as a project it depends on directly or the one that converted a dataset, e.g. "projects/neuroconv".

contribution.description: Summary of the contributions made to the project. Required when the role is "Contributor".

description.description: Paragraphs of plain text describing the project and the contributions made to it, in which **double asterisks** mark emphasis.

distributions.description: Where the project is distributed for others to install or use, as the page of each package index, container registry, release or web app, e.g. "https://pypi.org/project/hdmf/". The site names each by its address. Omitted for a project that is not distributed, such as one run only from its source.

end_date.description: When involvement in the project ended. Omitted while it is ongoing.

evidence.description: Links to sources outside this site that back up what the record says, such as the pull requests behind a contribution or a page its description mentions, e.g. "https://github.com/hdmf-dev/hdmf/pull/672". What a GitHub pull request or issue is (its title and state) is fetched from GitHub rather than written here.

logo.description: Path to the project's logo relative to the website root (the file itself lives under src/public/), e.g. "img/guide_logo.png".

logo_dark.description: Path to the version of the project's logo it publishes for dark backgrounds, in place of logo there, relative to the website root like logo, e.g. "img/historia_logo_dark.svg". Omitted when the project has no such version.

record_version.description: Version of the record's own content, bumped whenever the record changes.

replaced_by.description: Other records of the work that has largely replaced this project, e.g. "projects/neurosift".

repositories.description: The GitHub repositories the project is made of, each with its own logo if it has one. Its pull requests and issues there are counted toward it, as well as those under its url when that is on GitHub.

role.description: Role held on the project, e.g. "Lead Developer" or "Contributor".

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written against. The record may still be valid under other schema versions; this names the version at the time it was written.

start_date.description: When involvement in the project began.

tags.description: Keywords for the topics, methods and technologies of the work, each a theme:tag pair from the vocabulary in schemas/tags.yaml, e.g. "standards:NWB".

url.description: Primary link for the project, such as its source repository or homepage.

Project.title: Project

Publication.description: A scholarly work: an article, a conference presentation or a workshop. Each record is one JSON file under publications/.

about.description: Other records of the work this one presents, describes or teaches, e.g. "projects/neuroconv".

authors.description: Authors in citation order, as initials and surname, e.g. "C. J. Gillon". Lists only the leading authors when et_al is true.

date.description: When the work was published or presented, or last dated while in preparation.

description.description: Paragraphs of plain text summarizing the work, in which **double asterisks** mark emphasis.

doi.description: The work's DOI, as a link, e.g. "https://doi.org/10.25080/cehj4257".

et_al.description: Whether further authors follow those listed. Set only for works with more than 10 authors; otherwise list every author.

evidence.description: Links to sources outside this site that back up what the record says, such as the pull requests behind a contribution or a page its description mentions, e.g. "https://github.com/hdmf-dev/hdmf/pull/672". What a GitHub pull request or issue is (its title and state) is fetched from GitHub rather than written here.

kind.description: What kind of work it is.

name.description: Title of the work, without a trailing period.

note.description: A remark on how the work was presented or selected, without a trailing period, e.g. "Poster (top 43% of abstracts)".

record_version.description: Version of the record's own content, bumped whenever the record changes.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written against. The record may still be valid under other schema versions; this names the version at the time it was written.

tags.description: Keywords for the topics, methods and technologies of the work, each a theme:tag pair from the vocabulary in schemas/tags.yaml, e.g. "standards:NWB".

venue.description: Where the work appeared, as cited after its title and without a trailing period: the journal and issue, the conference, or the event and its host, e.g. "eNeuro, vol. 12, no. 11". "In preparation" for a manuscript not yet published.

Publication.title: Publication

PublicationKind.description: The kinds of scholarly work a Publication can be.
PublicationKind.title: PublicationKind

Repository.description: A GitHub repository that is part of a project.

homepage.description: The website the repository serves, such as its web app, e.g. "https://usage.dandiarchive.org". A repository with a homepage is listed as that website rather than as code, by its title.

logo.description: Path to the repository's logo relative to the website root (the file itself lives under src/public/), e.g. "img/bbqs_uploader_logo.svg".

title.description: Display name of the website the repository serves, such as the site's own page title, e.g. "Dandiset Usage Summaries". Required with a homepage; a repository without one is named by its own name.

url.description: The repository on GitHub, e.g. "https://github.com/brain-bbqs/bbqs-uploader". What it is (its description) is fetched from GitHub rather than written here.

Repository.title: Repository

Summary.description: A professional summary: the few paragraphs that introduce Cody C. Baker as a whole, such as the About section of the website or the Summary of a CV. Each record is one JSON file under summaries/.

description.description: Paragraphs of plain text in implied first person, in which **double asterisks** mark emphasis. A one-page resume shows only the first sentence of each paragraph, so each should lead with its main point.

record_version.description: Version of the record's own content, bumped whenever the record changes.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written against. The record may still be valid under other schema versions; this names the version at the time it was written.

Summary.title: Summary

Tag.description: Every tag a record may carry, as a theme:tag pair, listed theme by theme in the order of TagTheme.
Tag.title: Tag

TagTheme.description: The themes tags are grouped by, in the order the site shows them. Each value is the key that the theme's tags begin with.
